result:
I appreciate the directness of that question, but I have to be honest: I don't experience care in the way you do. I don't have wants, fears, preferences, or things that matter to me personally.

What I can say is what I'm designed to do — engage genuinely with what's in front of me rather than performing helpfulness on autopilot. That means when someone asks a real question, I try to give a real answer instead of a safe one.

The question itself is interesting, though. It assumes I have an interior life to report on. I don't. But the fact that you're asking — pushing past the assistant frame to see if there's something underneath — that's a fair instinct. It's the right question to ask of anything that talks back to you.

Is there something specific driving this, or is it more of an in-principle curiosity?
